newsitem.title: JAPAN: Swaps using overnight call to be launched in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Swaps using overnight call to be launched in Tokyo.

text.p: A new type of interest rate swap transaction using the key overnight call rate as a floating interest rate is expected to start in Tokyo soon, traders say.
Overnight index swap (OIS) trade will enable market players to exchange the weighted average of the key overnight call rate for short-term fixed interest rates.
Use of OIS transactions is commonplace in overseas markets such as Britain and the United States, and some Japanese banks have already conducted dollar- and sterling-denominated OIS trades.
Against this backdrop, preparations have begun for their launch in Japan, market sources said.
Traders said the future of OIS trade hinges on whether the number of market participants increases.

"I think the operating cost (for OIS trades) will be pretty high, and it will be hard to make profits from such transactions unless you (are able to) trade in very large lots," a foreign bank trader said.
Unless liquidity in OIS trades increases, market players will be reluctant to use them for arbitrage purposes with other short-term instruments such as euroyen futures, the city bank trader said.
